mode of production.context_notes: Formal Marxist category combining productive forces and relations of production. Use the English in parentheses on first occurrence.

surplus labor.context_notes: Essential political economy term; do not use casual words.

commodity.context_notes: In Marxian political economy 'माल' is the standard term for an object produced for exchange. 'वस्तु' is too broad.

feedback.context_notes: In cybernetic and systems engineering contexts, transliterate as फीडबैक.

algorithm.context_notes: Use modern transliterated Devanagari for computing terms.

proletariat.context_notes: Formal class category; it is not synonymous with all poor people or all wage earners in ordinary speech.

means of production.context_notes: Includes instruments of labour and objects of labour; do not reduce it to machinery alone.

productive forces.context_notes: Established historical-materialist term; includes labour power, knowledge, techniques and instruments of production.

relations of production.context_notes: Use for the social relations through which production is organized, especially property and class relations.

economic base.context_notes: Use with 'अधिरचना' when translating the base-superstructure relation.

superstructure.context_notes: Established Marxist term for political, legal and ideological forms related to the economic base.

dialectical materialism.context_notes: Retain the formal philosophical term; do not paraphrase it as a generic materialist outlook.

historical materialism.context_notes: Formal Marxist method for explaining historical development through material social relations.

contradiction.context_notes: In dialectical and political-economy contexts use 'अन्तर्विरोध'; reserve ordinary words for a simple inconsistency or disagreement.

use value.context_notes: Use the hyphenated technical term; it is not the same as utility in neoclassical economics.

exchange value.context_notes: Do not equate it automatically with market price.

value.context_notes: In the labour theory of value, translate as 'मूल्य'. Use 'कीमत' only for price.

price.context_notes: Keep distinct from Marxian 'मूल्य' (value), unless the source explicitly uses value in the ordinary non-technical sense.

labour.context_notes: Use the formal term in political economy; 'काम' may be suitable only in non-technical prose.

labour power.context_notes: A distinct Marxian category: the worker's capacity to labour, sold as a commodity under capitalism.

labour process.context_notes: Use for the process in which labour acts on an object through instruments of labour.

abstract labour.context_notes: Technical value-form category; do not paraphrase it as imaginary labour.

concrete labour.context_notes: Use as the counterpart of 'अमूर्त श्रम' in the analysis of the commodity.

socially necessary labour time.context_notes: Formal value-theory term; retain the full phrase.

surplus value.context_notes: Do not translate as profit. It is the value appropriated beyond the value of labour-power.

surplus labour.context_notes: Use for labour performed beyond necessary labour, not simply overtime work.

necessary labour.context_notes: Use in relation to the reproduction of the value of labour-power.

constant capital.context_notes: Marx's category of capital transferred to the product without creating new value; not merely fixed capital.

variable capital.context_notes: Capital laid out on labour-power that produces surplus value; do not confuse with circulating capital.

fixed capital.context_notes: Keep distinct from Marx's 'constant capital'. The English in parentheses is recommended on first use.

circulating capital.context_notes: Keep distinct from variable capital; the categories overlap differently.

organic composition of capital.context_notes: Formal term for the value composition of capital insofar as it reflects its technical composition.

accumulation of capital.context_notes: Use for the conversion of surplus value into additional capital.

primitive accumulation.context_notes: Formal Marxist term concerning the historical separation of producers from the means of production.

reproduction.context_notes: In political economy, use for the renewal of the conditions of production and social relations.

simple reproduction.context_notes: Reproduction on the same scale; retain the paired term with extended reproduction.

extended reproduction.context_notes: Reproduction on an expanded scale through accumulation.

turnover of capital.context_notes: Technical term for capital's circuit and the time required for its renewal.

rate of surplus value.context_notes: Do not merge with the rate of profit.

rate of profit.context_notes: Use consistently for the ratio of surplus value to total capital advanced.

tendency of the rate of profit to fall.term: tendency of the rate of profit to fall
tendency of the rate of profit to fall.preferred: मुनाफे की दर में गिरावट की प्रवृत्ति
tendency of the rate of profit to fall.context_notes: Translate as a tendency, not as an unconditional or mechanically universal prediction.

rent.context_notes: In Marxian agrarian political economy use 'लगान'; use 'किराया' for ordinary tenancy only when the technical category is not intended.

differential rent.context_notes: Formal category of rent arising from differences in fertility, location or investment conditions.

absolute rent.context_notes: Use as the counterpart of differential rent in Marx's theory of ground rent.

landed property.context_notes: Use for the social institution or form of property in land, not merely a plot of land.

monopoly.context_notes: Use the established modern political-economy term.

monopoly capital.context_notes: Use for capital organized under monopoly conditions.

finance capital.context_notes: Use for the Marxist-Leninist concept linking bank and industrial capital; do not reduce it to money capital.

imperialism.context_notes: Retain the established political-economy term. 'विस्तारवाद' is not an equivalent in Lenin's technical analysis.

bourgeoisie.context_notes: Formal class term. Use 'पूँजीपति वर्ग' only where the source specifically means the capitalist class rather than bourgeois society broadly.

petty bourgeoisie.context_notes: For a social stratum between the bourgeoisie and proletariat; 'निम्नमध्यवर्ग' may be used only if the source is explicitly sociological rather than Marxist-theoretical.

lumpenproletariat.context_notes: Keep the established term; do not turn it into a blanket moral description of poor people.

class struggle.context_notes: Established Marxist term for conflict rooted in antagonistic class relations.

class consciousness.context_notes: Use the hyphenated formal term, especially in Leninist discussion of political consciousness.

dictatorship of the proletariat.context_notes: Established Marxist term. Do not soften or replace it with a generic description of government; explain it in a note if needed.

revolution.context_notes: Keep distinct from a revolt, coup or reform unless the source uses those specific concepts.

reformism.context_notes: A political tendency; do not translate as a neutral individual reform.

revisionism.context_notes: Use for the established Marxist political-theoretical term; it is not identical to reformism.

opportunism.context_notes: Use the formal political term; 'व्यावहारिकता' is not equivalent.

social democracy.context_notes: Use the historical Marxist party and movement term. Keep English on first occurrence where the period matters.

social democrat.context_notes: Use the established historical-political term, especially for Lenin-era parties and activists.

socialism.context_notes: Established political-economic term; do not reduce it to welfare policy.

communism.context_notes: Use the established term for the Marxist social formation and movement.

anarchism.context_notes: A political doctrine, not a synonym for disorder.
